title: The curtain won't close
stem:
You are an F2 doctor on a general medical ward round. The consultant is examining Mrs Doherty, 76, who has had to lift her gown for an abdominal examination.

The curtain around her bed doesn't close properly, leaving a gap through which people in the bay and the corridor can see her. She looks uncomfortable.
instruction: Choose the 3 most appropriate actions to take in this situation.

options.text: Cover Mrs Doherty with a sheet as much as possible.
options.detailed: A sheet can cover her while the examination continues. It is a quick, simple way to reduce her exposure.

options.text: Carry on quickly to keep the exposure brief.
options.detailed: Speed doesn't address the gap, and a rushed examination may be less thorough.

options.text: Ask Mrs Doherty to hold the curtain closed herself.
options.brief: Unfair, and impractical during an examination.
options.detailed: She is lying down for an abdominal examination. It isn't her job to protect her own privacy.

options.text: Ask people in the bay to look away.
options.detailed: This draws attention to her and doesn't stop people seeing.

options.text: Close the gap in the curtain during the examination.
options.detailed: Standing in the gap, or holding the curtain closed, gives her privacy at once.

options.text: Complain to the estates department at the end of the week.
options.detailed: Reporting it is right, but waiting a week leaves the problem for other patients.

options.text: Report the broken curtain so it is fixed.
options.brief: Prevents the same problem for other patients.
options.detailed: A curtain that doesn't close affects every patient in that bed space. Reporting it gets it repaired.

options.text: Postpone the examination until a side room is free.
options.detailed: Simple measures can protect her privacy now, so there is no need to delay her examination.

explanation.issue: This tests whether you notice and fix a threat to a patient's dignity during a routine examination.
explanation.keyDetails: The curtain doesn't close. She is exposed and uncomfortable. Simple measures are available.
explanation.reasoning: [A] covers her, [E] closes the gap, and [G] gets the curtain fixed. The distractors rush ([B]), burden her ([C]), draw attention to her ([D]), delay the repair ([F]), or delay her care ([H]).
explanation.competing: [H] protects her privacy but delays her examination when simple measures would work.

references.title: Good medical practice
references.note: Domain 2, respecting patients' privacy and dignity.
